title: PerSeM: Persistent Semantic Memory for Long-Horizon Open-Vocabulary UAV Mapping
subtitle: Persistent 3D semantic memory for aerial perception
abstract: Open-vocabulary segmentation enables detailed semantic perception from UAV imagery, but independent frame-wise predictions can be inconsistent across viewpoints and time. PerSeM addresses this problem using persistent world-space semantic memory. Frame-level predictions are associated with 3D voxels to construct a majority-based semantic representation, which is subsequently refined through history-preserving spatial refinement, trust-aware replay, and context-guided verification. Experiments on Forest and UAVScenes demonstrate that persistent 3D aggregation substantially improves semantic consistency over frame-wise predictions. PerSeM further refines uncertain memory states, with improvements concentrated in challenging and temporally unstable regions, without retraining the segmentation backbone or introducing additional neural-network inference.
